settings.heading: Twelve formulas. No seasonal launches.
settings.text: We started because a friend with reactive skin could not find a cleanser that listed what was in it. Everything since has followed from that: short ingredient decks, published test data, and a range that only grows when a formula earns its place.
Products in the whole range, after seven years
Participants in our last twelve-week barrier study

settings.title: Short decks, printed in full
settings.text: If an ingredient cannot be justified to a customer in one sentence, it does not go in. Every carton carries the complete list at its real percentage.

settings.title: Concentration follows the evidence
settings.text: We formulate to the dose the literature supports, not the number that sells. That is why our niacinamide is 4% and not 10%.

settings.title: Fragrance-free unless there is a reason
settings.text: Fragrance is the most common avoidable irritant in skincare. Leaving it out costs us a pleasant first impression and gains reactive skin a product it can keep using.

settings.title: We publish what we measure
settings.text: Test data goes in the Journal — including the studies where the effect was smaller than we hoped.

settings.title: A cleanser, and nothing else
settings.text: Made in a rented lab in Almada for one friend with reactive skin, then for forty more.

settings.title: The barrier cream
settings.text: Ceramides and squalane at a ratio we reformulated nine times. Still our second-best seller.

settings.title: Moved to Sintra
settings.text: Our own GMP-certified line. Batch testing in-house from that point on.

settings.title: Leaping Bunny certified
settings.text: Audited supply chain, no animal testing at any tier.

settings.title: Twelve products
settings.text: Two launches a year at most. Anything that does not outperform what we already sell does not ship.

settings.heading: One lab outside Lisbon, batch-tested before it leaves.
settings.text:
We produce in a single GMP-certified facility in Sintra. Every batch is tested for microbial load and active concentration, and the certificate of analysis is printed on the carton with the batch number.

Nothing is tested on animals, at any stage, in any market — including the ones that would require it. That decision costs us distribution and we are keeping it.
